text:
maya: FYI customer (AcmeRetail) opened a support ticket — their overnight embedding job appears to have exhausted the monthly token bucket and then only partially refilled at reset. They say the job retried a lot due to 429s. Can someone triage?

quota-bot: Ticket created: #SUP-8243 (linked to thread).

ravi: Can you paste the job id + tenant/org id and the timeframe? Also need the last_request_id(s) if available.

maya: Job ID: job-2026-03-15-emb-77, tenant_id: acme-retail-prod, org_id: org-8942. Window: started 2026-03-15T01:12:03Z -> 2026-03-15T04:23:11Z. Customer reports visible bucket 0 at 2026-03-31T23:59:50Z then a partial refill (not full monthly amount) at 2026-04-01T00:00:05Z. They attached logs showing many 429s and long retry loops.

akiko: Which client lib/version were they using for embeddings? We had a known retry/idempotency change in the 1.2.x client. If retries don't preserve an idempotency key we can double-count retries as new requests.

maya: They sent this header example from their worker: 

```
POST /v1/embeddings HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***
Content-Type: application/json
# their worker omitted any Idempotency-Key header in the snippet
{ "model": "open-embed-1", "input": [ ... 512 items ... ] }
```

maya: Excerpt from their logs: 
```
2026-03-31T23:58:12Z -> 200 OK -> tokens: 512k
2026-03-31T23:59:01Z -> 429 Too Many Requests -> retry after 1s
2026-04-01T00:00:01Z -> 200 OK -> tokens: 512k
2026-04-01T00:00:02Z -> 200 OK -> tokens: 512k (duplicate)
```

ravi: Hmm that pattern looks like a retry window spanning the reset boundary. If each retry is treated as a new request (no idempotency key) the billing system will count every successful attempt, and we may see inflated token usage around UTC midnight. Our monthly bucket is refilled at 00:00 UTC, but requests that succeeded before/after will still be counted against the ledger.

akiko: Confirmed — I reproduced locally with a small script that retries on 429 without reusing a stable idempotency key. The server creates a new invoice line per accepted request. Example repro (pseudo):
```
for chunk in chunks:
  try:
    resp = post('/v1/embeddings', chunk)
  except HTTP429:
    sleep(1)
    resp = post('/v1/embeddings', chunk)
```
No Idempotency-Key -> two successful posts counted separately.

maya: Customer says total tokens consumed reported by API usage = 2.3M during the job window, but the billing ledger shows ~3.1M (extra caused by retry duplication). They saw their UI go 0, then at midnight the bucket showed +1.5M (partial refill) but not full because duplicates pushed ledger past the new bucket size.

ravi: Action items: 1) eng-runtime to add telemetry to detect when the same logical job ID results in multiple successful requests within a small time window (likely duplicate hits). 2) billing ops to reconcile + propose credit/refund. 3) docs/devex: call out idempotency header usage for long-run batch jobs.

akiko: Quick mitigation: client-side - recommend using Idempotency-Key: <job-id>-<chunk-index> for each chunk so retries map to same server request. Server-side longer-term: we should accept Idempotency-Key header and dedupe counting in billing if duplicates are from same idempotencyKey within X minutes. I'll open a PR.

billing-op: Pls provide the ledger lines and customer invoice. We can prepare a pro-rated credit once eng confirms duplication source. Also: we need a support note to explain partial visible refill vs ledger reconciliation.

maya: I already asked customer for the worker code and their retry config. They said "we used exponential backoff, max attempts 5, no idempotency." They're willing to have us test a one-off replay.

akiko: Found the offending code path in embeddings handler: when a 429 occurs client-side retry, the server updates usage when the request completes; there is no check for duplicate idempotency-key header today. PR to add dedupe and a short cache of seen idempotency keys (store request_id -> tokens, TTL 10m) -> will prevent double counting across retries that complete after reset.

ravi: Timeline? This affects any long-run batch that crosses UTC midnight and has retries. Severity medium-high for billing.

akiko: I have a minimal patch in review: link to PR: https://git.internal/redwood/embeddings/PR-4812 (notes: safe, feature-guarded behind config flag). If merged we can enable for Hosted customers and then consider Dedicated.

maya: Customer update posted: asking for ETA and if we can refund provisional amount.

billing-op: I'll prepare a provisional credit for the visible overcharge and flag it as pending until eng confirms duplicate detection.

ravi: Also add a monitoring alert to flag >20% token variance between api-usage and billing-ledger over a 1h window around UTC rollover for any tenant. That will catch regressions.

maya: Great. I'll keep the ticket updated. Thanks all :thumbsup:

[thread end]
